persona: Nurse transcribing medication administration from handwritten ward notes; not data-savvy
source_style: hand-typed from paper MAR (medication administration record) into CSV, multiple data entry shifts

columns.name: PatCode
columns.notes: W-NNNN format; some rows blank (merged cell simulation)

columns.name: Time_Administered
columns.notes: three formats: HH:MM (24h), H:MM AM/PM (12h with space), HH.MM (dot)

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: free text or blank; inconsistent capitalization

clean_table.generation_rule: 70 rows: i from 1-70; PatCode=W-(4200+i) or blank if i≡0(mod 11); MedicationName cycles through 12 variants; Dose=250,500,750 (pattern i%3) or 5-7 for mL (if i%5==0); DoseUnit=mL if i%5==0, blank if i%7==0, else mg; Time_Administered: three formats by i%3 (24h HH:MM, 12h H:MM AP, dot HH.MM); NurseInitials from 7 options or lowercase if i%13==0; Notes cycles through 11 options

intended_analysis: Identify medication administration times (requires parsing 3 time formats); detect missing dose units; flag duplicate or missing patient codes; calculate doses by medication; audit administration patterns
mess_applied: Three different time formats (HH:MM, H:MM AM/PM, HH.MM dot notation)
Missing dose units in ~1/7 of rows
Blank PatCode cells (simulating handwritten merged cells)
Free-text Notes with inconsistent capitalization and punctuation
No standard order or structure beyond headers
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A naive reader would parse all time values as text, miss the pattern in blank codes, and fail to standardize medication names or normalize dose units—resulting in duplicate and unintelligible medication names and unparseable times.
